issuer_or_brand: UK consumer law (GOV.UK guidance for retailers)
program_name: UK consumer rights on faulty goods (GOV.UK: Accepting returns and giving refunds)
jurisdiction: UK (the page states 6 years to make a claim, 5 years in Scotland)
core_standard: A retailer must repair or replace an item that was faulty when bought; the customer has the same right to free repairs or a replacement whether or not a warranty or guarantee exists or has run out
mandatory_conditions: The claim is made against the retailer that sold the item
Proof of purchase from that retailer (receipt, bank statement or packaging)
The item was faulty when it was bought
The claim is made by the person who bought the item
exclusions_and_caveats: This is the period to make a claim, not a 6-year warranty
After 6 months, the retailer can ask the customer to prove the item was faulty when it was bought
In Scotland the period is 5 years, not 6
A refund may not be owed if the customer knew about the fault when buying or damaged the item by trying to repair it (repair, replacement or a partial refund may still apply)
